requirement_text.REQ-202: Content-addressed artifact store (repository_artifacts, artifact_versions) plus a SEPARATE REPO-04 canonicaliser, deliberately NOT an extension of REQ-036's promotion digest. Ported from R-Co migrations/045_repository_artifacts.sql. Full text read from docs/requirements.yaml lines 11158-11302.

task.description: CODE-DESIGNER (WF-02 Step 1) for REQ-202. Wrote lib/letflow/design/req202-artifact-repository.md covering the two-table content-addressed store, the migration-058-vs-045 conflict, the separate canonicaliser module, create/2 dedup+versioning semantics, DB-level immutability, REQ-067 cursor pagination for version history, and the REQ-041 name-collision disambiguation.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-202's 14 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete design element (design doc section 10 traceability table)
No implementation code -- signatures/type shapes only, no .ex/.exs code fences, no literal SQL
Tenant-scope placement decision (per-tenant vs global) stated with explicit reasoning, REVIEWER-flagged if global
Canonicaliser is a separate module from promotion_digest.ex with required moduledoc cross-reference recorded
DB-level immutability mechanism specified (not just app-level absence of update)
Open questions listed explicitly rather than silently resolved

result.summary: Design places both repository_artifacts and artifact_versions PER-TENANT (Decision 0003-B default), NOT global -- diverging from R-Co's own effectively-global store. Reasoning: no acceptance criterion requires cross-tenant dedup, Decision B's own stated rationale is physical blast-radius isolation (not storage efficiency), cross-tenant byte-identical collisions are not a realistic workload for tenant-authored config/business-logic artifacts, and going global would be S6's only unforced divergence from Decision B. Consequence stated explicitly: dedup (REPO-01) is per-tenant only, a deliberate forfeiture of cross-tenant storage savings. Because this follows Decision B rather than diverging, NO REVIEWER sign-off flag is raised. New Letflow.Repository.Canonicaliser module (lib/letflow/repository/canonicaliser.ex) built separate from PromotionDigest, confirmed by direct source read that PromotionDigest.canonicalize/1 passes all numbers through unchanged (no normalization), while REPO-04 requires normalized integer-valued-float forms -- merging would silently break every stored promotion digest (INV-PRM-5). Required moduledoc cross-references specified on both modules. DB-level immutability via a per-tenant-schema trigger (copied from req195-audit-entry-storage.md's precedent) raising 'repository_artifacts is immutable' / 'artifact_versions is immutable' on UPDATE (and DELETE for repository_artifacts). Version history reuses Letflow.Api.Pagination's REQ-067 cursor contract verbatim. REQ-041's solution_pack_artefact_bases explicitly disambiguated as an unrelated global install-tracking table. Migration ships R-Co migration 045's shape only; migration 058's conflicting shape (version_id PK, TEXT content_hash, inline content_json) recorded as a defect not to port. Four open questions flagged: OQ-1 (exact decimal form for non-integer floats), OQ-2 (tension between recommended PromotionDigest moduledoc amendment and AC5's literal 'not modified' wording, checked by git diff --stat), OQ-3 (exact JSON content-type match set), OQ-4 (artifact_id generation/semantics, caller-supplied vs server-derived).
